rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper describes the preprocessing pipeline.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: The anatomical images were first bias/field corrected and segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid using the SPM12 (http://www. fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/ spm) toolbox. Then, CT estimation was further performed by the DiReCT (diffeomorphic registration-based cortical thickness) algorithm available in ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools) (38). As suggested by Schwarz et al. (39), SPM12 segmentation input to ANTs thickness (SPM 1 DiReCT) method was the most reliable of all the thickness-based measures. Finally, the resulting CT maps were modulated and resampled into 2 3 2 3 2 mm using the DARTEL (Diffeomorphic Anatomical Registration using Exponentiated Lie algebra) algorithm (40).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear mixed-effects models were used to investigate the effects of group and sex on ACC CT. Post hoc tests with FDR correction were used for simple effects.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Sex determines anterior cingulate cortex cortical thickness changes over the course of major depressive disorder, with females showing thinner ACC CT overall, and different patterns of thickness changes in first-episode versus recurrent MDD compared to males.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Females showed thinner ACC CT compared to males across all groups. Female patients with a first depressive episode had significantly thinner ACC CT compared to male patients with a first episode. Male patients with a first episode showed thicker ACC CT compared to both male patients with recurrent MDD and healthy males. These differences were primarily in the perigenual and subgenual ACC, not the dorsal ACC.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The findings suggest the need for early and prolonged sex-specific clinical interventions targeting stress regulation.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study is cross-sectional, not longitudinal. The dataset is from a single country (China). Information on the number of depressive episodes, duration of treatment, age of onset for the recurrent group, and early adverse events was not available. Subtypes of depression could not be distinguished.
